claims.note: Title and meta description only; they state this article's own subject and scope (a 2026 review of the replay-based local tool agentperf-local, package version 0.3.3). No external numeric claim and no first-party result.

Opening answer summarises the README's own definition of the tool (replays recorded conversations against an OpenAI-compatible server, reports throughput and latency, measures speed without measuring output quality) and the vendor announcement's framing; the statement that nothing about output quality is measured is quoted from both.

Reviewer-verified: task/turn counts, the `exact` output policy and the ~58,000-token largest turn are quoted from the project README ('The default run', 'Context requirement'); the ~56K context growth in the same paragraph is the vendor announcement's own wording ('context grows to ~56K tokens'). Both sources were re-fetched on 2026-10-15 and the quoted strings matched.
Six-turn synthetic `aa-mini-v1` replay and its documented non-comparable status quoted from README 'The default run'; no run of it is asserted here beyond what the documentation states.

Documentation boundary, stated as a scope limitation: the eight recorded tasks are the vendor's set and are not enumerated in the documentation we read, so the workload cannot be reconstructed from public docs alone. This is not a claim that the workload is invalid.

All four bullets are the vendor's published figures (73-93% KV-cache-served prompt tokens, 22-41% prefill share for Qwen3.8-27B, ~196K new input against ~31K output tokens, 24 s / 39 s / ~2 s tool-return pauses) reproduced and explicitly labelled VENDOR RESULTS. No independent replication was performed.

65,536-token full-context requirement at batch size 1, the 131,072 alternative, the `reduced: true` non-comparability rule and the 8,192-token mini fallback are quoted from README 'Context requirement'.

`ignore_eos` being outside the OpenAI API, the pre-run check that stops and names the flag, and the Ollama case (cannot honour `ignore_eos`, switches to the `recorded` policy, normalized latency estimate not directly comparable) are quoted from README 'Attached servers'.

The arm64-only SWE-bench validation image script and the live-mode caveats (untrusted recorded commands, Docker not a security boundary, read-write workspace, no network by default) are quoted from README 'Real tool calling'.
Documented `managed-run` invocation with a catalog profile and framework flag, copied from the README quick-start examples; it is a command recipe, not a measured result.
Recipes as per-model/per-hardware YAML files, SHA-256 verification of downloaded files, and the Splash 1.2.1 / `incoai/Qwen3.8-27B-Splash` commit pin are quoted from README 'Quick start'.
Launch hardware set, launch model set, 4-bit quantizations and 14 speculative-decoding serving configs are the vendor's published rows, labelled VENDOR RESULTS; no row was reproduced by us.

Vendor's own findings (active-parameter ranking, 5090 >3.5x completion and >5x decode, Spark vs Halo 1.4-1.7x, MacBook within 2-9% and 21% slower on Qwen3.5-9B, speculative decoding 30-120% above roofline, MSRP/price statement) reproduced as VENDOR RESULTS with the vendor's memory-bandwidth figures.

Author-run bounded smoke run, disclosed as a harness reproducibility check and explicitly not a hardware benchmark: 6/6 turns, 0 failures, 5 tool calls, 67.5 s measured replay time, on stated hardware with stated versions. The run file is the measurement record of exactly this run; see the run methodology for the exact command and scope limits. Reviewer re-hashed this run record from the tree (hash matches) and re-ran the recorded command once in private scratch; the guards reproduced, so no new first-party performance claim is created by this approval.

run.methodology: Bounded harness reproducibility check run on 2026-10-15T00:12:32Z..00:13:46Z: `uv tool install agentperf-local` (0.3.3), `agentperf-local run --base-url http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1 --model qwen2.5:0.5b --replay aa-mini-v1 --no-progress --timeout-seconds 180` against Ollama 0.20.3 on an aarch64 box (2 vCPUs, ~12 GiB, no supported accelerator).
